Description: Fragments of a Hebrew copy of Ecclesiastes (Qohelet) from Qumran Cave 4, among the oldest Dead Sea Scrolls found at Qumran. The surviving text covers parts of chapters 5-7, including the well-known saying that sorrow is better than laughter (Ecclesiastes 7). It is the larger of the two Qumran Ecclesiastes copies: the published count gives it about 125 words against about 21 for 4Q110 (4QQohb, Ecclesiastes 1:10-15).
ImageCredit: Osama Shukir Muhammed Amin — CC BY-SA 4.0
Significance: Pushes the Hebrew text of Ecclesiastes back to the mid-2nd century BC, centuries before the medieval manuscripts, and shows the book already in circulation in essentially its familiar form. Its variants against the Masoretic Text are minor in character; its importance is its age and its confirmation of the book's early transmission, not a rival text of Ecclesiastes.
